newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil strike hangs on gov't - union.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil strike hangs on gov't - union.

text.p: Venezuela's main oil union Fedepetrol said it was still considering calling a strike unless the government confirms no jobs will be lost in restructuring at state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).

Fedepetrol president Carlos Ortega said this strike was a separate issue from the national stoppage called by the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV) on August 6, in which Venezuela's 60,000 oil workers would participate.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Ortega said he planned next week to meet the Ministry of Energy and Mines, which has to approve the restructuring, to demand a clause stating that jobs would not be shed in the move.
"If the Ministry guarantees no jobs will be lost in the restructuring, then there will be no strike," he said.
PDVSA president Luis Giusti said on Tuesday that the restructuring would not lead to any job losses. Indeed, he expected PDVSA to create 10,000 new jobs next year alone.

The company is planning to dissolve its three vertically- integrated subsidiaries Maraven, Lagoven and Corpoven to create three new horizontal business units. Giusti said the move would bring $12 billion added value in net present terms over ten years, after the $300 million costs.
Ortega thought up to 12,000 jobs could be under threat, but Giusti said added value, rather than lower costs, was the main thrust behind the changes.
